comments.body:
Implementation design settled after reading ADR 0112 + the existing admission seam (recorded here rather than in the description, which is under the 8,000-char plan-review admission cap).

**Seam.** `rebar.llm.peak_rss.gate_peak_rss` is already a context manager wrapping exactly the scope S6 needs, and its own docstring states the reason: "Wrapping the library entry points (`review_plan` / `verify_completion`) rather than the MCP daemon and the CLI separately covers both call paths at one seam, since both reach the gate through these functions." Admission takes the same seam — a sibling context manager in `rebar.llm.gate_admission`, entered immediately outside `gate_peak_rss` in `review_plan()` and `verify_completion()`. One wrapper, both gates, both AC4 paths, one shared counter.

**Counter.** N slot files under the snapshot store's existing `locks/` directory (`store_root()/locks/gate-slot-<i>`), each held with a non-blocking `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` for the duration of the run and released in a `finally`. This is cross-process (AC4: CLI runs are separate processes) and crash-safe by construction (AC5: the kernel drops a flock when the holding process dies or its fd closes — no PID heartbeat, which ADR 0005/the janitor already rejected as unsound). It also serialises correctly between threads of one process, because a `flock` is held by the open file description and each acquisition `open()`s its own. It inherits `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, so it follows gate scratch onto ADR 0112 decision 3's dedicated volume for free.

**Refusal.** `GateCongestedError` — an exception, never a verdict value, so it cannot be mistaken for INDETERMINATE or a BLOCK (AC3). CLI maps it to **exit 11**, the code this repo already documents as "transient — retry", rather than minting a new one. MCP returns a structured `{error: ..., retryable: true}` payload in the same shape `_structured_llm_failure` already produces, so a driving agent branches on `retryable` instead of parsing English.

**Metric (AC7).** A one-line `GATE_CONGESTED {json}` stderr marker, copying the `GATE_PEAK_RSS` / `VOTER_ERROR` / `MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR` convention verbatim. That convention exists precisely because the containers hold no AWS credentials and the host probe greps journald; it is also the portable choice (`project.portability`) — it works identically under the CLI on a laptop with no CloudWatch and no CI provider.

**Config (AC6).** `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates`, resolved by a new `resolve_gate_max_concurrent` alongside `resolve_gate_min_free_bytes`. `0` disables the bound (the off-switch idiom `max_bytes`/`max_entries` already use); a malformed value falls back to the default rather than crashing every gate, matching `resolve_gate_min_free_bytes`'s stated posture.

**Deliberate deviation from ADR 0112 decision 6 — no `REBAR_GATE_*` env tier.** The ADR asks for `REBAR_GATE_* env > [snapshot] > default`. The env tier is omitted. `scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_config.py` censuses `REBAR_*` literals as the `env_var` kind, so a new `REBAR_GATE_MAX_CONCURRENT` is a new mechanism — and bug `a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a` records that a new mechanism is currently **unlandable**: a `# mechanism-ok:` marker satisfies `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` but `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py::test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree` asserts `new == 0` regardless of markers, and every route to the baseline is closed to a contributor. The `[snapshot]` table itself is a `_RESERVED_SECTIONS` member and so is not in `_SECTIONS`, which is what the `config_key`/`feature_flag` detectors read — confirmed against `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`, which holds zero `config_key::snapshot.*` entries. The config tier therefore lands cleanly today and the env tier can be added in one line once `a1f1` is fixed. Filed here so the gap is a recorded decision, not an oversight.

**Default = 4.** Derived from the measurements this epic already took, not guessed. Per-gate resident cost: plan_review `peak_rss_bytes` ~748 MB, verify_completion ~462 MB (`GATE_PEAK_RSS` markers; ADR 0112 cites ~739 MB / ~4.7 min, and a degraded run at 501 MB, so the figure varies run to run). The host is a `t4g.large` (8 GiB) shared with Gerrit, and ADR 0112 decision 7 forbids growing it. Steady state is ~2.17 GB and Gerrit reserves ~3 GiB by config (`heapLimit 2g` + `packedGitLimit 1g`), leaving roughly 3 GiB for concurrent gate work. 4 x 748 MB ~= 2.99 GB fits inside that; a fifth concurrent run (~3.74 GB) does not. 4 is also decisively below the operator's stated ~10 concurrent plan reviews, which is the point — a cap at or above observed peak sheds no load and bounds nothing.

comments.body:
Implemented and pushed as Gerrit change **2609** (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2609).

Plan review PASSED and signed on the sixth pass (`head_sha 83359f2249873f942648326d044016b39b8c8162`); the run's own `build_drift` line reported the worktree build 2 commits behind the pinned ref, confirming it was the checkout build and not the ~195-commit-stale global install. The five earlier BLOCKs, and what each changed:

1. **G1G2 / T8** — the plan asserted an exit-11 / retryable-payload mapping without stating `GateCongestedError`'s place in the hierarchy, so the mapping was not guaranteed to fire. Fixed by making it a direct `LLMError` subclass carrying a retryable `LLMOutcome(WAIT_AND_RETRY)`, which routes it through the `except LLMError` arms that already exist. This *shrank* the change: `_mcp_llm.py` needed no edit at all.
2. **prerequisite-consistency** (twice) — the reviewer compares against the ADR text pinned on prerequisite 7dfa, an earlier three-decision draft, while the merged `docs/adr/0112-*.md` on `origin/main` has seven. Resolved by citing decisions by HEADING rather than number.
3. **G6** — "fail open on every plumbing failure" silently disarms the cap. Fixed by announcing it: a `GATE_ADMISSION_DISARMED` marker on every degraded admission.
4. **E4** — the seam was described in terms that fit `plan_review` only; `verify_completion` spends bytes in `_resolve_completion_ticket_view` too. The wrapper encloses the whole remainder of that function.
5. **G6 again** — the fail-open posture contradicted the ADR's own consequence that admission must treat an unreachable scratch volume as a REFUSAL, "not as an empty cache to repopulate onto the root filesystem". Split: local faults (no `fcntl`, one bad slot file) admit + announce; an unreachable store root refuses with `GateScratchUnavailableError`.

**One implementation deviation from the reviewed plan.** The plan said no new `except` clause was needed on either surface. That held for MCP and for `verify-completion`, but `_cli/_llm_commands._review_plan` hardcodes `return 1` for an `LLMError` rather than calling `_llm_error_exit_code` (its sibling handler does). Found by the AC3c test going RED at `assert 1 == 11`. It gets one narrow arm ahead of the generic one, catching only the two admission refusals; existing `LLMError` behaviour on that path is untouched.

**RED-first evidence.** Tests landed before the implementation and failed at `ImportError: cannot import name 'gate_admission'`. After implementing: 26 passed, 1 failed — the CLI exit-code case above — then 27/27 green. Two mutations proved the tests have teeth: widening the slot scan to `limit + 1` turned 10 tests RED (including both cross-process cases and both entry-point wiring cases); dropping the `finally` around `release_slot` turned the slot-release-on-failure case RED with a `GateCongestedError` on the follow-up admission. Both restored.

**Ratchets.** None fired. `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports `active=682 new=0 increased=0 stale=0` and `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` is 31/31 green — no marker, no baseline edit. The design avoids registering a mechanism name at all: the cap is a `[snapshot]` key (a reserved section, absent from the `_SECTIONS` the config detectors read), the slot files reuse the store's existing `locks/` directory, and there is no new `REBAR_*` literal. Complexity ratchet: `active=35 new=0 increased=0 stale=14`.

Two `make lint` gates did fire and were fixed properly: `gen_env_registry --check` (a line-number shift in `docs/env-vars.md`, regenerated) and `check_wall_clock_asserts.py` on the AC2 fast-fail timing assert — sanctioned inline as a hang-guard, since the only alternative behaviour (a blocking, queueing acquire) never returns at all while the holder is inside its `with`, so the ceiling dwarfs the expected wall time rather than sitting just above it.

Full verification: `make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` "Success: no issues found in 755 source files", targeted suite 32/32, and a regression sweep of 2623 unit tests (`-k "plan_review or completion or llm or mcp or config_resolver or errors or snapshot"`) all passing.

compiled_state.description:
# S6 — Bounded concurrent gate executions, with fast-fail admission

Implements the decision headed **"Bounded concurrency with FAST-FAIL admission (S6)"** in the
LANDED `docs/adr/0112-on-box-disk-ceiling-architecture.md` on `origin/main`. Decisions are cited
by HEADING, never number: prerequisite 7dfa records an earlier, shorter Decision list whose
numbers do not match the merged file.

## Why

S2–S5 cap each accumulator with a high-water-mark GC, and **a watermark GC assumes evictable
data exists**. The janitor takes no per-reader lease and relies on POSIX delete-on-last-close,
so it may `unlink` an in-flight snapshot but the blocks return only when the last reader closes.
Under the operator's **~10 parallel plan reviews** the held bytes are LIVE, not garbage: the GC
finds nothing evictable and the volume fills anyway. Both gates copy the repo at a ref and share
**ONE counter** (two caps of N each admit 2N); at capacity the call **fast-fails**, since a
queued gate still holds its thread, ~739 MB resident, and the client's request.

## Design

**Seam.** `peak_rss.gate_peak_rss` already wraps this scope and says why: wrapping
`review_plan()` / `verify_completion()` "covers both call paths at one seam, since both reach
the gate through these functions". Admission takes that seam but sits strictly OUTSIDE it, since
`gate_peak_rss` wraps only the run while the bytes are spent earlier. It becomes the **outermost
`with`** in each entry point, enclosing every byte-spending step: in `review_plan`,
`resolve_gate_handle(...)` plus the run; in `verify_completion` it must open before
`resolve_gate_handle` AND enclose `_resolve_completion_ticket_view` (which materializes the
pinned ticket store and may rebind `handle`) plus the `try/finally` closing that view — the
whole remainder of the function.

**Counter.** N slot files in the store's existing `locks/` dir, each held for the run under a
non-blocking `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`, released in a `finally`. Cross-process (AC4) and
crash-safe (AC5: the kernel drops a flock when the holder dies — no heartbeat, which the janitor
rejected as unsound). It also serialises across threads of one process, since a flock is held by
the open file description and each acquisition opens its own; and it inherits
`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, following gate scratch onto the ADR's dedicated volume.

**Degradation is SPLIT**, per the ADR's consequence that admission must treat an unreachable
scratch volume as a refusal, not "an empty cache to repopulate onto the root filesystem":

- **No `fcntl`, or one slot file unusable inside a healthy `locks/` dir** — ADMIT, and emit one
  `GATE_ADMISSION_DISARMED {json}` marker naming the reason. Refusing would turn a platform gap
  into a total gate outage, and the free-space floor still applies; but a silently disarmed cap
  is how bug 3276 recurs, so it is never silent.
- **The store root unreachable** (scratch volume unmounted or read-only, so `store_root()` /
  `locks/` cannot be created) — **REFUSE**, with `GateScratchUnavailableError` (same `LLMError`
  base and retryable outcome, its own `gate_scratch_unavailable` code). Admitting would silently
  relocate gate scratch back onto the root filesystem — the failure this epic prevents. No
  marker: a raised refusal already reaches the caller and its log.

**Refusal — the hierarchy decides the mapping.** `GateCongestedError` lives in
`src/rebar/llm/errors.py` as a **direct subclass of `LLMError`** (not `LLMRunnerError`: no
runner ran) and attaches `.outcome = LLMOutcome(WAIT_AND_RETRY, retryable=True)` in `__init__`.
Those two facts fire the mapping through arms that ALREADY exist, so **no new `except` clause is
added**:

- MCP: `_review_plan_body` / `_verify_completion_body` catch `rebar.llm.LLMError` →
  `_structured_llm_failure`, which reads `outcome_of(exc)` (`getattr(exc, "outcome", None)`), so
  the attached outcome gives `retryable: true` (without it, `false`), and no `verdict` key is
  emitted — congestion is unreadable as INDETERMINATE, BLOCK or FAIL.
- CLI: both handlers catch `llm.LLMError` → `_llm_error_exit_code`, returning **11** ("transient
  — retry") exactly when `outcome.retryable`, else 1, after an `Error:` line.
- `_errors._llm_error_code` gains branches for both new types returning `"gate_congested"` /
  `"gate_scratch_unavailable"`, in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`, placed **before every existing arm** (the
  bare `isinstance(exc, LLMError)` would otherwise report them as `command_failed`). The
  error-taxonomy contract test asserts the family is EXHAUSTIVELY mapped, so both are registered
  there too — it verifies this in-session.

**Metric (AC7).** One line-start `GATE_CONGESTED {json}` stderr marker per refusal, following
the `GATE_PEAK_RSS` journald convention (the containers hold no AWS credentials) — also
portable: identical under the CLI with no CloudWatch and no CI provider.

**Config (AC6).** `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates`, resolved by `resolve_gate_max_concurrent`
beside `resolve_gate_min_free_bytes`. `0` disables the bound (the `max_bytes` idiom); a
malformed or negative value falls back to the default rather than disarming the cap. No
`REBAR_GATE_*` env tier, deviating from the ADR's measured-defaults decision: a new `REBAR_*`
literal is a new `env_var` mechanism, unlandable today per bug `a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a`, while
`[snapshot]` keys are exempt (`_RESERVED_SECTIONS`, absent from `_SECTIONS`).

**Default = 4, from measurement.** `GATE_PEAK_RSS`: plan_review ~748 MB, verify_completion
~462 MB (the ADR cites ~739 MB and a degraded run at 501 MB, so it varies). The host is a
`t4g.large` (8 GiB) shared with Gerrit and the ADR's host-sizing decision forbids growing it;
~2.17 GB steady state plus Gerrit's ~3 GiB reservation leave roughly 3 GiB for gate work.
4 × 748 MB ≈ 2.99 GB fits; a fifth run (~3.74 GB) does not — and 4 is well below the observed
~10 concurrent, so the cap actually sheds load.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: one counter bounds both gates — hold `limit` slots as `plan_review`, assert a
  `verify_completion` admission is refused.
- [ ] AC2: the refused call returns in under one second while a holder still runs (it
  fast-fails rather than blocking or queueing).
- [ ] AC3a: the message names host congestion and says to retry; on the review-bot path this is
  ADR 0069's retryable deferral, never an `LLM-Review −1`.
- [ ] AC3b: not readable as a verdict — the MCP body returns `retryable: true`,
  `error == "gate_congested"`, and NO `verdict` key.
- [ ] AC3c: the CLI returns exit 11 on a congestion refusal.
- [ ] AC4: a real child process holds every slot; this process is refused.
- [ ] AC5a: SIGKILL a holder, assert a later admission wins (no lost slot).
- [ ] AC5b: raise inside the wrapper, assert the next admission succeeds.
- [ ] AC6a: the cap reads `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates`, defaults to 4, treats 0 as off, and
  falls back to the default on a malformed or negative value — one test each.
- [ ] AC6b: `docs/config.md` and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` both name the key, default and
  rationale; the latter says a congestion refusal is an expected outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] AC7: a refusal emits exactly one `GATE_CONGESTED` marker naming gate, ticket and limit; an
  admitted gate emits none.
- [ ] AC8a: with `fcntl` unavailable the gate is admitted AND one `GATE_ADMISSION_DISARMED`
  marker naming the reason is emitted.
- [ ] AC8b: with `store_root()` raising, the gate is REFUSED, not admitted.

## Testing & file impact

`pytest tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py -q`, the taxonomy contract test, `make lint`,
`make typecheck`, `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q`.

New: `llm/gate_admission.py`, `tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py`. Edited: `llm/errors.py`,
`llm/plan_review/__init__.py`, `llm/completion.py`, `_config_resolvers.py`, `_errors.py`, the
taxonomy contract test, `docs/config.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. Unchanged: `_mcp_llm.py`,
`_cli/_llm_commands.py`.

file_impact.reason: the MCP admission point: _spawn_gate_daemon starts gate work on an in-process daemon thread, so the counter must be acquired here before a run starts and released when it ends, including on the failure path

plan-review library entry point — one of the two operations that snapshots the repo at a ref and therefore consumes the bounded resource; CLI runs reach the gate through here, not through the MCP daemon
verify_completion entry point — the second consumer sharing the same counter, per the operator's decision that both operations contend for the same disk
declare the concurrency limit as a config key with a measured default; a new config key trips the shrink-only mechanism ratchet and needs an in-tree mechanism-ok marker naming this ticket
document the key, its default and the rationale for that default, per AC6

the oracle: limit+1 executions rejects the last; the rejection is immediate rather than blocking; the error shape is distinguishable from a gate verdict over both MCP and CLI; crash-safe slot reclamation; and metric emission on rejection

compiled_state.title: S6 — Fast-fail gate admission above a configurable concurrency cap
